ships.title: Ship 1 — DeepSeek RAG (originally AWS SageMaker, rebuilt locally)

lookbook.narrative: Ship 1 was the first attempt — AWS, DeepSeek, a RAG pipeline built to organize my own life. It got lost. The notebook wasn't on the SageMaker instance. It wasn't in the backups. I rebuilt it from the Mirror files. The rebuild was cleaner than the original. That's the ship that taught me how to recover from losing one.

By the time Ship 2 came, I was more confident. I had rebuilt Ship 1 from scratch. I understood what I was capable of and what the tools could do. Ship 2 was IBM Granite — a different model, a cleaner notebook, and a new layer: agentic reasoning. I learned to write clean code and I learned what agency meant. This is the ship where I stopped being a student and started being a builder.

Ship 3 runs locally with IBM Granite as the model. Same pattern, different model. If the design only worked with one LLM, it wasn't real. This is the ship that proved the pattern was portable — not locked to AWS, not locked to DeepSeek, not locked to anything.

Ship 4 combined IBM Granite with agentic reasoning. Retrieval plus action, on the second platform. This is the ship where I learned that agency wasn't a feature — it was a way of thinking about how a system works. Cross-platform and agentic, together.

ship7.title: msgvault adapter
ship7.receipt: Smoke run 1: 200 msgs, 23,500 chunks; run 2 resumed at row 201 — never re-ingest

lookbook.narrative: The seventh ship bridges mail into the Mirror. It reads msgvault.db in its own native tongue — the embed_gen watermark is its checkpoint, so progress lives in the data itself: crash, restart, curfew, resume, never re-ingest. It normalizes RFC822 message-ids, preserves full metadata, and feeds the canonical store with nomic-embed-text vectors — the fleet's model. Replace-mode: stale deleted as fresh lands. Curfew-aware. Never self-restarts. The prior-art search found nothing published like it.

lookbook.toc_child: DV14™: The Box · AI containment blueprint
lookbook.narrative: A concept, stated plainly: a physical and conceptual AI agent containment architecture, designed to answer one question — can an agent that runs on hardware be contained by hardware? Two tracks: The Box (eight layers of complementary opposites — every material paired with the one that covers its weakness) and the Sensory Deprivation Matrix (can an agent function with no external hardware at all?). The accidental discovery: if the AI plays possum, we have found a holding cell. Bitcoin-timestamped September 19, 2026. Cited in two published white papers. © all rights reserved — commercial license only; Bitcoin-timestamped 2026-09-19; available for review under NDA.

lookbook.toc_child: Radiology Companion™ · v5 reference build — architecture sealed
lookbook.narrative: The ninth ship is sealed. The fleet proved that a sovereign archive can hold a person's records without surrendering them — Radiology Companion™ asks the next question: can the same local-first doctrine carry a patient through a clinical protocol? An imaging patient-preparedness tool: the imaging protocol explained in order, the preparation steps verified, no cloud, no stored health data, nothing about the patient leaving the device. Pitched as a 90-day fixed-fee pilot against the institution's own reschedule baseline. On October 22, 2026 — seventeen days after the decline — it was built anyway: Radiology Companion™ v5, a working local-first reference build. Twenty languages. Every preparation step read aloud. A hospital's own name and logo, fetched from a pasted link. Four sourced institutional demo libraries. Built with no funding. Demo free, deploy paid. Source private; the architecture is sealed — commercial license only, available for review under NDA.

ship10.title: Ship 10 — Overseer™
ship10.status: built 2026-10-11 — working quorum orchestrator; paper published same day

lookbook.narrative: The tenth ship is the one that watches the others. Overseer™ dispatches every question to five workers — three vector collections, the SQLite mail archive, and the canon registry — fuses their findings with a visible quorum table, and refuses to answer when the receipts are insufficient. Its tier system settles the oldest problem in AI: when the model lies, the pipeline decides. Canon questions never reach the model at all.
